headline: Running streak ties personal best at 20 weeks while lactate threshold data points to strong aerobic ceiling.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The 20-week streak is the headline structural achievement right now — not just as a number, but as evidence of sustained, consistent stimulus across a wide range of effort levels. Volume is essentially flat week-on-week, but flat volume with consistent execution across easy, moderate and threshold efforts is a productive state, not a plateau. The 44 km effort from mid-June is still influencing the picture here — that kind of load takes time to fully absorb, and the two recent easy runs sitting comfortably at sub-6:00 pace with modest HR suggest absorption is progressing well.

The lactate threshold marker from yesterday — 4:24/km at 178 bpm — is the most meaningful single data point this week. Without sufficient history to contextualise it against a 30-day baseline yet, it can't be trended, but it aligns with your half-marathon PB trajectory and confirms the aerobic ceiling is operating at a high level. That's the kind of marker that validates the base you've been building across the streak, not just the recent weeks.

Strength is the one area worth a quiet note — four sessions in the last four weeks against what appears to be a higher prior rate. Not a concern at this volume, and the current profile remains strong, but it's worth keeping the frequency up as weekly running load sustains or grows.
watch_items: The lactate threshold figure will become much more valuable once a few more test points accumulate — worth noting whether pace at threshold continues to hold or improve across July.
Easy-run HR has dropped noticeably vs the prior period; watch whether this continues to trend down or stabilises, as it's one of the cleaner real-time fitness signals available.
Strength frequency has dipped — monitor whether it naturally recovers in the coming weeks or whether running load is consistently crowding it out.

The 20-week streak is now at its all-time best; no action required, but worth being attentive to any early signs of accumulated fatigue (motivation, sleep quality, unusual soreness) as you move into new territory.
